reason: The command advisory overlay enforced its minimum assisted-latency floor with max(floor, reduced_latency). If an indigenous formation already had latency below that donor floor, applying command support could increase its latency and therefore reduce supported command service below the indigenous baseline.
Stage-3 task 444 (cell log_08, seed 2026120000) exposed the defect by correctly tripping the strict formal-domain invariant: formal service external must be nonnegative.
The v4 freeze did not hash rust/pineland-model/src/movement.rs even though that file implements command-support dynamics. The v5 freeze closes that provenance gap.

command_latency_monotonicity.old_behavior: assisted_latency = max(indigenous_latency * (1 - reduction_fraction), donor_floor), which could be larger than indigenous_latency when the indigenous path was already faster than the donor floor.
command_latency_monotonicity.new_behavior: assisted_latency = min(indigenous_latency, max(indigenous_latency * (1 - reduction_fraction), donor_floor)), after nonnegative clamping. Assistance may improve latency or leave it unchanged but may never directly worsen the indigenous baseline.

freeze_coverage.new_behavior: rust/pineland-model/src/movement.rs is a required cryptographically hashed artifact in the v5 production freeze.

scientific_invariants.simulation_dynamics_change_scope: bug fix restoring the preregistered monotonic interpretation of external command assistance

rationale: Unlike the v4 runtime-only telemetry/safeguard changes, this correction can alter simulated movement-order timing and downstream state trajectories.
The triggering condition occurs at the individual formation/order level and cannot be proven absent from a completed shard using the aggregate telemetry alone.
Therefore no v3/v4 shard is reused in the final v5 scientific dataset; all 720 discovery worlds must be rerun under one v5 commit and freeze.
